title: DashboardBooks
description: Books dashboard data consumed by the books widget. The books array is a simplified display projection of LP books-export data with DS-added fields (isbn, link, progress). bookMeta, statusLabels, and stats are DS-owned additions with no LP equivalent.

books.description: List of books projected from LP books-export, augmented with DS display fields. Field set is a subset of LP's books items plus DS-specific additions (isbn, link, progress).

isbn.description: ISBN-13 (or Kindle ASIN when no ISBN exists) used as a stable key into bookMeta.

asin.description: Amazon ASIN used for affiliate link construction and as an alternate key into bookMeta.

status.description: Reading status key. Must match a key in statusLabels.

rating.description: User rating 1–5 stars, or null if unrated.

progress.description: Reading progress as a percentage (0–100). 0 for unstarted, 100 for completed.

bookMeta.description: Supplementary metadata keyed by isbn (or ASIN for Kindle-only titles). Provides series, genre, page count, year, and description for each book in the books array.

seriesName.description: Series name if part of a series, null otherwise.

seriesNumber.description: Position within the series, null if standalone.

seriesTotal.description: Total number of books in the series, null if standalone or unknown.

desc.description: Short plot or synopsis description used in the book detail panel.

statusLabels.description: Human-readable display labels keyed by status value. Maps status enum values to UI strings.

next.description: Label for books queued to read next.

in_progress.description: Label for the book currently being read.

stats.description: Aggregate reading statistics computed by the DS pipeline.

totalRead.description: Total number of books with completed status.

upNext.description: Number of books queued with next status.

avgRating.description: Average star rating across all rated books.

booksThisYear.description: Total books started or completed in the current calendar year.
